stem: A 7-year-old child has severe localised hip pain, fever and refusal to walk; which diagnosis must be considered as an orthopaedic emergency?
explanation: Septic arthritis is the orthopaedic emergency to consider in a child with severe localised joint pain, fever and inability to weight bear.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: The Limping or Non-Weight-Bearing Child

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because transient synovitis is usually a less serious cause of limp and does not explain the combination of fever, severe localised pain and refusal to walk as well as septic arthritis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because acute myositis may cause pain and limp, but it is not the orthopaedic emergency suggested by fever with severe localised joint pain.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because septic arthritis is an orthopaedic emergency and should be considered when a child has severe localised joint pain, fever and refuses to walk.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because benign growing pains do not cause fever, marked localised hip pain or refusal to bear weight.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a simple ankle sprain does not fit a febrile child with severe localised hip pain and inability to walk.
